methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Cabinet secretary: Southside county loses two economic development prospects due to uncertainty over data center taxes
signals.signal_reading: Policy uncertainty blocking data center investment in Greensville County demonstrates how Southside regions remain vulnerable to capital flight even when pursuing AI infrastructure, reinforcing concentration in established hubs rather than enabling distributed economic opportunity.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-funded community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia signals potential for deep, locally-rooted AI capability development through peer networks rather than top-down platform deployment, directly addressing coal-transition communities' need for distributed skills.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's institutional partnership with AI Ready RVA concentrates AI education infrastructure in the Richmond metro hub, likely creating deep capability among university-adjacent populations while raising questions about knowledge transfer to rural Virginia.

signals.title: State invests $3M to help transform Hampton Roads into hub for aircraft technology and training - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: State investment transforming Hampton Roads into an aircraft technology hub deepens the region's specialized AI/defense tech capability, reinforcing Virginia's multi-nodal concentration pattern rather than broad distribution across smaller communities.

signals.title: When AI imagines cities, smaller communities can disappear - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech research showing AI-generated urban imagery erases smaller communities reflects how algorithmic systems may systematically disadvantage rural Virginia in investment, planning, and recognition—accelerating the visibility and resource gap between metros and periphery.
